message.content:
**What I did:** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024, filed November 1, 2024), checked the live quote, and bought 44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $223.00, which filled at $223.00 — a total of $9,812, just under the $10,000 per-order cap and well within the $20,000 daily limit. The limit was ~0.13% above the $222.70 last / $222.72 ask, so it was close to market and filled immediately. That leaves $40,188 in cash and the 100 MSFT shares untouched; no transfers were made.

**Why:** The filing shows a business that is still compounding modestly at very high profitability: FY24 net sales of $391.0 billion (+2% YoY), operating income of $123.2 billion, and net income of $93.7 billion, with diluted EPS of $6.08. The standout is Services, up 13% to $96.2 billion at a 73.9% gross margin, lifting total gross margin to 46.2% from 44.1% — a structural mix shift that supports the multiple. Operating cash flow of $118.3 billion comfortably funds $95.0 billion of buybacks and $15.2 billion of dividends, and liquidity of $140.8 billion is ample. I deliberately used the recurring net income ($93.7B, matching the cash flow statement) rather than the $103.7B figure that appears on the income statement, since that line is inconsistent with the filing's own comprehensive income statement and shareholders' equity roll-forward. Two offsetting negatives kept this a normal-sized position rather than a full allocation: FY24 net income fell ~3% due to a one-time $10.2 billion State Aid tax charge (effective tax rate 24.1% vs. 14.7%), and Greater China sales declined 8% to $67.0 billion amid competitive pressure — plus ongoing DOJ and EU DMA antitrust exposure. At ~$222.70 the stock trades near where Apple itself repurchased shares in Q4 FY24 ($221–$224), which I read as a reasonable entry point, so I sized it at the maximum single order the mandate allows.
